claim: NEAR Intents is taking a growing share of on-chain trading
test: Intents volume over the DEX volume of the six peer chains in the last three complete months, over the same share in the three months before, minus 1 (fct_intents_unit_economics_monthly, fct_peer_daily)
why_this_threshold: Any gain counts. Quarters are compared and not years, because a year earlier Intents had barely started and a yearly gain would flatter it

claim: Intents volume was at least $2B in each of the last three complete months
test: The lowest volume_usd of the last three complete months (fct_intents_unit_economics_monthly)
why_this_threshold: The bar the author's earlier draft of this thesis named as what would change its author's mind (the near-deflation-clock scaffold; see the README's disclosures)

claim: NEAR's wallets receive a rising share of the fees charged on Intents
test: Revenue over fees in the last three complete months, minus the same in the three months before (fct_intents_unit_economics_monthly)
why_this_threshold: Any rise counts. Three months are read together because revenue is swept in lumps, so one month alone can sit far from the trend

claim: More partners pay meaningful fees than a quarter ago
test: Partners with at least $10,000 of app fees in a month, counted over the last three complete months, over the same count for the three months before, minus 1; swaps that name no partner are left out (fct_intents_channel_economics_monthly)
why_this_threshold: Any growth counts. $10,000 a month is the size at which a partner is a business and not a trial

claim: The revenue NEAR reports arrives on chain: what its wallets received is within 10% of its own monthly series
test: One minus what the Intents contract paid the revenue wallets, with USDC at one dollar on the day it arrived and NEAR at the transfer's value, over revenue.near.org's monthly revenue series, all time (fct_wallet_transfers, fct_revenue_page_monthly)
why_this_threshold: The bar the author's earlier draft of this thesis named as what would change its author's mind (the near-deflation-clock scaffold; see the README's disclosures)

claim: The revenue wallets keep the NEAR they receive: under 5% of it has left
test: NEAR sent out of the three revenue wallets, not counting moves between them, over NEAR they received (fct_wallet_flows_daily, fct_revenue_inflows_daily)
why_this_threshold: Small enough to be operations rather than selling

claim: The Bitwise ETF took in more NEAR than the chain created over the last 30 days
test: flow_to_issuance_30d_ratio on the newest trading day (fct_etf_absorption_daily)
why_this_threshold: More than issuance means a ratio of at least one. The 30 days count the fund's flow on its trading days and the issuance on every day. The same ratio since the fund's first trading day is cumulative_flow_to_issuance_ratio in the same table; it is not the test because with no flows at all it stays above one for months, so it says little about demand today

claim: Burn and the NEAR the revenue wallets receive are a larger share of issuance than in the 90 days before
test: Gas burned plus NEAR received by the revenue wallets, over NEAR created, across the 90 days to the newest settled day, minus the same across the 90 days before (fct_net_dilution_daily, three 30-day readings each)
why_this_threshold: Any rise counts. Ninety days are read to smooth single months. The base is the 90 days before, because a year earlier the wallets had received nothing and issuance was twice as high, so against that base the claim could not fail

claim: The unlock schedule is spent: under 1% of supply is still locked
test: 1 minus circulating_share_of_total on the newest day: what lockup contracts and the two Foundation lockup accounts still hold, over total supply (fct_circulating_supply_daily)
why_this_threshold: Under a hundredth of supply is too little to move the float. The test does not cover NEAR the Foundation holds unlocked, which is not published. Lockups whose owners never switched transfers on (19.35M NEAR, unchanged since July 2023) count as unlocked, as in NEAR Explorer; counted as locked they would put the share above the bar

claim: At the end of HSP-029's ramp to 1.6%, a doubling of Intents volume would let revenue and burn match the NEAR that is created
test: breakeven_volume_multiple for scenario hsp029_end_state at the measured share of fees (fct_deflation_scenarios)
why_this_threshold: A doubling is the bar the claim names

claim: NEAR's application fees grew faster than the median peer's over the last three complete months
test: Change in application fees, the last three complete months against the three before, for NEAR minus the median of the six peers (fct_peer_daily). Quarters are compared and not years, because a year earlier NEAR's fees had barely started and a yearly gain would flatter it. The Market page's question on fee growth shows the fastest peer, the 90-day and the yearly figures beside it
why_this_threshold: Faster than the median peer means a gap above zero. The median of the six peers is the yardstick the valuation claim uses, so growth and price are held against the same peer. Until 2026-11-14 the claim read the fastest of the six: on those quarters NEAR and Solana grew within a point of each other, so the result turned on which nightly read of the fees was scored. Against the median the gap was below zero at the quarters ending June and July 2026, so the claim can fail

claim: NEAR trades above the median peer on application fees
test: NEAR's multiple on the app_fees basis over the median of the six peers', on the newest settled day (fct_valuation_multiples_daily). A year of fees is the last 30 days times 365/30, and each market cap is as its source reports it
why_this_threshold: Above the median means a ratio over one

claim: One partner supplies more than half of 1Click's fees
test: The largest partner's share of 1Click app fees over the last three complete months (fct_intents_channel_economics_monthly)
why_this_threshold: More than half is what dependence on one partner means

claim: Zcash is on one side of at least a fifth of 1Click volume
test: Share of finished 1Click volume with ZEC as origin or destination, over the last three complete months of the daily run (fct_intents_1click_pair_daily)
why_this_threshold: The published share of ZEC alone was 9% of all volume; a fifth on either side is the bar for dependence. Three months are read together because the share moves by ten points from one month to the next

claim: Fewer accounts sign transactions on NEAR than six months ago
test: Mean distinct_signers over the newest 30 days over the 30 days ending 180 days earlier, minus 1 (fct_chain_daily). Accounts that only signed their own deletion are left out while NearBlocks /v1 reports them, which ends on 2026-11-22. More than four in five of them call one game, HOT's, over the 30 days to 2026-11-11 (fct_bigquery_contract_daily), so this count follows its players
why_this_threshold: A tenth fewer signers in half a year is a fall and not noise. Signers are read and not transactions, because the count of transactions without the batch streams was only lower with the Sweat relayer in it, and Sweat Wallet is due to end on 2026-12-30

claim: A growing share of NEAR's transactions are sent to NEAR Intents
test: Transactions sent to intents.near over all transactions on the chain in the last three complete months, minus the same share in the three months before, as NEAR's public BigQuery dataset counts them (fct_bigquery_receiver_daily, fct_bigquery_chain_daily). A month is complete when the dataset has been read for every day of it
why_this_threshold: Any rise counts. Three complete months are read against the three before, as for every claim about Intents. The count comes from the chain's public record and not from NEAR's own volume series, so it tests the growth of Intents on a second source. The two batch streams that once filled most of the chain's transactions ended in April 2026, so from the three months to October 2026 both sides of the comparison count the same kind of traffic. The share fell at the quarters ending February to April 2026, so the claim can fail

claim: The ten largest pools hold more than a third of the stake
test: The ten largest staking pools' share of all stake in the newest complete epoch (fct_validator_summary). These are pool accounts: the data does not record who runs a pool
why_this_threshold: The chain stops finalising if over a third of the stake goes offline or refuses, so that much in ten pools is the bar for concentration. The share was under a third on 16 of the 365 days to 2026-11-10, last on 2026-01-14, so the claim can fail. It replaced a claim on the number of validator pools on 2026-11-12: the pools that left in 60 days held under 1% of the stake, and the count moves by a dozen between two epochs of one day

claim: Less NEAR sits in liquid staking than a year ago
test: NEAR staked through the liquid staking tokens stNEAR, LiNEAR and rNEAR on the newest day, over the same day a year earlier, minus 1 (fct_lst_snapshot)
why_this_threshold: Any fall over the year counts. Liquid staking is where the chain itself shows holders keeping NEAR at work, and what it pays halved when issuance was cut in October 2025. The figure was above zero until July 2026, so the claim can fail

claim: Dollars held in NEAR Intents are higher than a quarter ago
test: Mean value of stablecoins held in NEAR Intents, public and confidential balances together, over the last three complete months, over the same mean for the three months before, minus 1 (fct_dune_intents_tvl_asset_daily)
why_this_threshold: Any rise counts. Three complete months are read against the three before, as for every claim about Intents, so a dashboard that is read on request cannot leave a month half measured. The series is NEAR's own figure. The stablecoins the contract holds are read from the chain at each month end, and the two agree at every month end since the dashboard has carried every stablecoin the pool holds (intents_pool_dollars_month_ends_chain_vs_dune in dq_reconciliation)

claim: Intents volume leads network usage: usage rises in the weeks after volume does
test: Not settled: the test finds no lead and has too few weeks to rule one out. The largest correlation between week-on-week changes in Intents volume and in four usage measures one and two weeks later (fct_usage_lead_correlations) is inside the 0.37 that chance alone gives with about 30 weekly changes. It is a common hypothesis about NEAR, which also asks whether volume leads better than the token price; the same table holds the price
why_this_threshold: Until 2026-11-14 this was scored as a claim for the case with a bar of 0.37, the most that chance alone gives, and it failed. It was moved here because a result inside the band of chance settles nothing either way, and because the hypothesis asks whether one series forecasts another, which is neither a link of the case nor a risk to it

claim: NEAR AI has paying users
test: Not testable: NEAR AI publishes no usage or revenue figures, and its one on-chain trace, escrow.ai.near, has a single caller

claim: A few market makers fill most Intents volume
test: Not testable: no public source gives counts or shares of market makers; the data here holds only the distinct callers of intents.near

claim: The NEAR Foundation's liquid NEAR is a large overhang on the float
test: Not testable: the Foundation's last published holding is 305M NEAR on 2024-01-11 (registry/near_supply_readings.csv); nothing newer is public

claim: Other cross-chain swap protocols are as large as NEAR Intents and can take its flow
test: Not testable: the services that do the same job do not report one kind of volume. Some report the swaps they settled and others the tokens sent through them across chains, which counts a transfer of the same token too, so whether one is as large as NEAR Intents depends on which kind counts (fct_swap_services_daily). The Intents page sets them side by side
